data.body:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (session: Copilot CLI, worktree mantis-atomic-fold).

Design: intent-journal (commit-pending sentinel) crash atomicity, per the epic's amended child bullet.

1. New module src/rebar/_commands/compact_recovery.py:
   - write_intent(tracker, ticket_id, snapshot_path, fold_files): atomic JSON record {ticket_id, snapshot (tracker-relative), sources (tracker-relative)} under <git-dir>/rebar-compact-intents/<ticket_id>.json — OUTSIDE the worktree, so the sentinel can never itself be tree dirt.
   - discard(journal): idempotent unlink.
   - pending_intents(tracker), recover_abandoned_folds(tracker) [caller holds the store write lock], recover_abandoned_folds_locked(tracker) [acquires it only when journals are pending].
   - Recovery discrimination: a journal whose snapshot is already in HEAD = crash between commit and journal removal -> discard only. A journal whose snapshot is uncommitted = abandoned partial fold -> rename *.retired sources back, unlink the uncommitted snapshot, git reset the ticket dir (unstage a crash-after-add), discard. The retained SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state (incomplete rollback in _retire_folded_sources) has NO journal by construction, so recovery never touches it — fsck --repair-snapshots stays its sole owner.

2. compact_txn._compact_locked: extract the mutation tail into _apply_fold() which (a) writes the intent journal before the first worktree mutation (when committing), (b) wraps snapshot-write -> retire -> commit in try/except with whole-fold rollback on ANY exception or commit failure (rename-back + snapshot unlink + unstage), (c) discards the journal on every completed outcome including both _retire_folded_sources failure returns. Recovery preamble runs inside the lock at fold start.

3. compact.py sweep: _sweep_one_ticket stops passing --no-commit (unless the operator passed it to compact-all), so each fold commits as ONE unit inside its own locked section — a killed sweep strands at most zero dirty folds instead of an entire uncommitted batch. compact_all_cli runs recover_abandoned_folds_locked() as its preamble. _commit_backfill still runs as a safety net but now pushes even when nothing is staged (per-ticket commits mean the batch stage is normally empty).

Withheld-oracle tests (written FIRST, confirmed RED) in tests/unit/test_compact_crash_atomicity.py: kill the fold (raise) at each intermediate step and assert `git status --porcelain` is clean; simulate SIGKILL (journal left behind) and assert the next sweep/compact converges the tree; assert recovery is idempotent; assert a successful fold still compacts and leaves no journal; assert the retained-SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT path is NOT reverted by recovery.
